figures.caption: Figure 7: C2V for Scene Appearance Editing. Keeping the ego actions and the dynamic/static elements fixed, we vary the text prompt to edit global appearance, including locale (e.g., , Germany vs. China), time of day (sunset vs. night), and weather (sunny vs. rainy). All images are generated by X-World, including the first frame.
Figure 3: The training pipeline of the proposed X-World.

Figure 6: Long Sequence Generation (24 s Multi-Camera Rollout). X-World produces temporally stable and view-consistent multi-camera videos over a 24 s horizon, supporting streaming longhorizon simulation without catastrophic drift.
Figure 1: (a) Spatial layout of the seven camera sensors. (b) Distribution of ego longitudinal actions.

Figure 4: Action Controllability. Each row shows a pair of logged and generated videos. The ego trajectories for the next 3s are overlaid in blue. Dynamic traffic participants are not constrained in this experiment and are generated freely by X-World. Top: Turn Right → Turn Left; Middle: Go Straight → Turn Right; Bottom: Lane Keeping → Lane Change.
Figure 2: The overall scheme of the proposed X-World.

Figure 8: Closed-loop simulation and counterfactual testing with X-World. Scenario 1: In the logged video, the ego vehicle waits behind a front car that is actually parked. Under the same initial scene, X-World enables counterfactual rollout to evaluate a policy that detours around the parked car. Scenario 2: Starting from a logged straight-driving scenario, we edit the scene by inserting a cyclist darting out from behind an occluding black car. X-World generates realistic futures under this edit, and the tested policy safely stops before the cyclist to avoid collision.

Figure 5: Dynamic and static element controllability. Projected bounding boxes of dynamic agents and road elements are overlaid on the videos. Green denote objects. Red lines denote solid road boundaries, and cyan lines denote lane markings.
